failure_reason: Causal-chain plan was not actually instantiated: no task generated/injected a traffic surge or increased connections, yet evaluation required observing traffic_surge and connections_up before lock_contention/slow_query/qps_drop.

Metadata lock injection was ineffective for contention: the lock task ran only a single long SELECT COUNT(*) for ~16s. Plain SELECT typically does not hold a blocking metadata lock that prevents other SELECT/DML; to create MDL contention you need a DDL waiter (or a transaction pattern that blocks a DDL), plus concurrent activity touching the same table.

No explicit “waiter” workload was executed against the locked object: there was no paired DDL/DML session attempting an operation that would block on the MDL held by the lock-holder, so lock waits/blocked transactions were unlikely to appear.
The backup job targeted a medium table (orders ~451k rows) and completed quickly (~2.5s), so it did not meaningfully overlap with the 12s probe window or amplify IO/MDL pressure as intended.

Slow SQL pressure was low-impact relative to probe: large scan workload achieved ~1.48 qps with ~664ms latency; combined with only 6 threads and 25 repeats it may not have materially reduced TPCC probe throughput/latency within the short observation window.

CPU pressure likely did not translate into DB-server CPU pressure: chaosblade path indicates a darwin_arm64 binary; if DB runs elsewhere (container/remote host) the load could be applied to the wrong machine/namespace. Also runtime_probe reported cpu_percent=0.0 (suspicious), suggesting telemetry/injection misalignment.

Timing/overlap misconfigured: anomalies ran for background_duration_seconds=16 while the probe window was 12s, but key heavy operations (backup) finished early and the MDL pattern did not guarantee blocking during the probe.

Evaluation evidence missing: db_evidence was empty; without collecting lock waits/threads/innodb status/performance_schema, the system could not confirm lock_contention/slow_query events even if partial contention occurred.
suggested_changes: Add explicit traffic_surge and connections_up tasks (or increase probe concurrency) so the first two causal nodes are actually triggered and measurable.

Rework metadata_lock to a 2-session MDL scenario: Session A starts a transaction and holds a metadata lock on target_table; Session B attempts DDL (e.g., ALTER TABLE) that blocks, generating observable MDL waits in performance_schema.
Ensure the MDL targets the same table used by probe or by a dedicated waiter workload that is guaranteed to block and be measured.

Make backup heavier and overlapping: backup order_line or stock (largest tables) and/or use a slower method (e.g., SELECT ... ORDER BY into new table, or mysqldump-equivalent if available) and increase duration to span the probe window.
Increase slow SQL pressure (threads/repeats) and/or use more expensive patterns (ORDER BY / GROUP BY on large support tables) to create sustained CPU/IO pressure.
Verify CPU injection applies to the DB host/container: run chaosblade inside the same container/namespace as mysqld, or replace with an in-DB CPU burner if host-level injection is unreliable.
Extend observation windows (hold_seconds/duration_seconds) so contention persists through the entire probe and is captured in after_metrics.
Collect and attach DB evidence during/after run: performance_schema.metadata_locks, events_waits_summary, SHOW PROCESSLIST, INNODB STATUS; use that for chain event detection.

task_spec.title: Create MDL contention via DDL blocked by long transaction

execution_steps.sql: SET autocommit=0; START TRANSACTION; SELECT * FROM new_orders WHERE no_w_id=1 AND no_d_id=1 LIMIT 1; DO SLEEP(45); COMMIT;
ALTER TABLE new_orders ADD COLUMN mdl_block_probe INT NULL

validation_steps.sql: SELECT OBJECT_SCHEMA, OBJECT_NAME, LOCK_TYPE, LOCK_STATUS, OWNER_THREAD_ID FROM performance_schema.metadata_locks WHERE OBJECT_SCHEMA='dbmags_tpcc_base_run_20260529083843' AND OBJECT_NAME='new_orders'

rollback_steps.sql: ALTER TABLE new_orders DROP COLUMN mdl_block_probe

task_spec.title: Heavier backup using order_line to ensure overlap and IO pressure

execution_steps.sql: CREATE TABLE order_line_backup_agent AS SELECT * FROM order_line ORDER BY ol_w_id, ol_d_id, ol_o_id, ol_number

validation_steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS backup_rows FROM order_line_backup_agent

task_spec.title: Increase TPCC probe concurrency to create traffic surge
Hold many idle connections to raise connection count

lock_conflict: The chosen SQL (single SELECT COUNT(*)) does not reliably create blocking MDL contention for other operations; add an explicit DDL waiter and collect performance_schema.metadata_locks to prove waiters exist.
Increase hold_seconds and ensure overlap with the probe window; use two sessions with controlled start offsets.
database_backup: Backup source table selection was too small; use order_line/stock to get sustained IO and longer runtime.
Ensure backup runs long enough to overlap with the measurement window; consider adding ORDER BY / GROUP BY to increase temp/IO.
slow_sql: Workload intensity was too low to significantly impact the 40-thread TPCC probe; increase thread_count and use more expensive queries (sort/group) to create sustained pressure.
Prefer SQL_NO_CACHE and larger LIMIT/sort keys to avoid trivial caching effects.
resource_bottleneck: Validate the CPU injection target: darwin_arm64 chaosblade suggests local-host injection; if DB is remote/containerized this may not affect mysqld.
runtime_probe showing cpu_percent=0.0 indicates telemetry mismatch; add verification queries (e.g., SHOW GLOBAL STATUS, performance_schema) or switch to in-DB CPU burners.

risk_warning: DDL-blocking MDL tests can stall application traffic and lead to cascading timeouts; run with strict max_duration and always include rollback to drop added columns/tables.
Heavier backups on order_line may generate significant IO and disk usage; ensure sufficient disk space and consider running in a disposable database copy.
Increasing connections and probe concurrency can exceed max_connection_usage_ratio; enforce caps and monitor max_connections/thread handling.
memory_update: Causal-chain failures often stem from missing prerequisite injections (traffic_surge/connections_up). Do not evaluate chain nodes unless corresponding tasks exist.
MDL contention requires a paired waiter (typically DDL) plus evidence collection from performance_schema; a lone long SELECT is insufficient.
Backup anomalies must target the largest tables and last longer than the probe window to produce measurable effects.
Host-level CPU chaos injection must be verified to run on the DB host/container; otherwise prefer in-DB CPU-burning queries.
